problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t+{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{8}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the velocity of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (12{t}^{5}+5{t}^{4})\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{6}+{t}^{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2({1}^{6})+{1}^{5}+C \\ 6 & =3+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{6}+{t}^{5}+3.$
